analysis: All changed files are under provider-swift/Tests; none are production sources. Changes examined: (1) EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift, where the helper switch now also handles the new `.toolCallDelta` case alongside `.toolCall`. The head excerpt covers only test bodies, with no security-relevant behavior change. (2) SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift, a comment-only update on maximumPrefillChunk. The logic is unchanged (dense Qwen 4096, others 2048). (3) GemmaOpenRouterLiveTests.swift, where the live-test harness now reassembles streamed OpenAI tool-call fragments keyed by index. It is an `.enabled(if: gemmaTestsEnabled)` test with no secrets, network endpoints or trust-boundary interaction. (4) GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift, which adds an exhaustive-switch case recording an issue if a `.toolCallDelta` is streamed for a named tool_choice. No threat-model assets (A-001, A-003, A-016 and others), trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011) or the T-041 prefix-cache surface are touched. The test-only changes weaken no authorization, attestation, encryption or cache control. Remaining integration question, outside the supplied batch: the production source change that introduced the `.toolCallDelta` stream event and streamed tool-call fragments is not visible here. Other batches should check that streaming partial tool-call deltas does not bypass the E2E encryption or fail-closed behavior in T-008, or leak tool arguments in plaintext. This batch gives no evidence of a regression.
